title: Declarative parameter profiles and human-first diagnostic messages for tool calls
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a compact, runtime-friendly declarative DSL for describing tool/function parameter profiles and a mapped set of human-first diagnostic messages. Goal is to reduce runtime validation surface (fewer full-JSON-schema parses), improve error clarity for integrators, and make remediation steps actionable in SDKs and the Console.
acceptance_criteria: A compact parameter profile DSL spec doc (<= 2 pages) that can express required/optional fields, basic types, enums, length/number ranges, and stable aliases for backward compatibility.
Runtime validator that converts DSL -> lightweight validation plan (no full JSON Schema at runtime) used by hosted and dedicated runtimes.
A canonical error taxonomy and message templates (error code + short message + remediation + link to docs) for all validation failure classes.
SDKs (JS + Python) surfaces the human-first error objects with remediation hints and example input fixes.
Integration tests covering common failure modes and end-to-end tests in the function-calling playground demonstrating messages in Console and API responses.
implementation_plan: Draft DSL grammar and examples (this ticket).
Prototype validator library that compiles DSL -> validation plan (Go + Rust prototypes).
Add mapping layer to runtime to attach error codes and remediation templates (runtime-2.2).
Coordinate SDK changes: error object shape and helper to render remediation (JS + Python).
Ship documentation and Console support (linkable remediation IDs).
Rollout: start with feature-flagged endpoint; collect telemetry and iterate on wording.
technical_decisions: Use a compact DSL instead of full JSON Schema at runtime to reduce parsing overhead and control UX surface.
Keep canonical JSON Schema as an authoring/export option for partner integrations; we will provide a compile target from DSL -> JSON Schema for compatibility.
Error codes are stable strings with a small namespace: 'VAL_' prefix for validation, 'TYPE_', 'MISSING_', 'FORMAT_', 'RANGE_'.
Each error response includes: code, short_message, remediation_hint, example_fix (when possible), and doc_url.
tradeoffs: DSL reduces expressivity vs. JSON Schema (no arbitrary 'anyOf' combinators). We accept this to keep runtime validation fast and messages consistent.
Maintaining a compiler between DSL and JSON Schema adds engineering cost but preserves interop with existing authoring tooling.
Human-first messages require iteration and localization later; initial rollout will be English-only with telemetry for refinement.

example_error_messages: VAL_MISSING_REQUIRED: 'user_email' is required. Remediation: include 'user_email' in your call (string). Example: {"user_email": "alice@example.com"}. Docs: <doc_url>
VAL_INVALID_TYPE: 'limit' must be a number between 1 and 200. Remediation: provide an integer value. Example: {"limit": 50}.
VAL_ENUM_MISMATCH: 'mode' value 'fastish' is not allowed. Allowed values: ["fast", "balanced", "accurate"]. Remediation: pick one of the allowed values.
VAL_FORMAT_EMAIL: 'owner' does not look like an email address. Remediation: use a valid email (name@domain).
VAL_DEPRECATED_FIELD: 'maxTokens' is deprecated; use 'token_limit' instead. Remediation: migrate to 'token_limit' before deprecation date 2026-08-01.
schema_dsl_sample:
# DSL sample lines (each line is a field declaration)
user_email: string required format=email description='Recipient email'
mode: enum{fast,balanced,accurate} optional default=balanced description='Inference quality mode'
limit: int optional min=1 max=200 default=50 description='Max results to return'
metadata: json? optional description='Freeform metadata; small payloads only; use structured fields where possible'
# Field modifiers: alias(old_name), deprecated(yyyy-mm-dd), stable (indicates no breaking changes)
